script.title: He jumped from a hijacked jet in 1971 and vanished
script.hook_text: He jumped out of a jet
sentences: On Thanksgiving Eve 1971, a passenger jumped out of a jet.
He'd paid cash for a one-way ticket to Seattle, as Dan Cooper.
His note to a flight attendant went into her purse unopened.
So he whispered, "Miss, you'd better look at that note. I have a bomb."
In Seattle he swapped the passengers for $200,000 and four parachutes.
Back in the air, he lowered the rear stairs and jumped.
In 1980, a boy building a campfire on a Columbia River beach found $6,000 of it.
The rest of the money was never found.
script.description:
Thanksgiving Eve 1971: a man named Dan Cooper hijacked a 727 with a note.
He jumped with $200,000 and was never identified.
visuals: D. B. Cooper ransom money found 1980
claims_en: On November 24, 1971, Thanksgiving Eve, the hijacker was on board Northwest Orient Flight 305, a Boeing 727, and later parachuted from it.
He bought a one-way ticket with cash to Seattle using the name Dan Cooper.
He handed a note to flight attendant Florence Schaffner, who dropped it unopened into her purse.
He whispered, 'Miss, you'd better look at that note. I have a bomb.'
In Seattle he released the passengers after receiving $200,000 ransom and four parachutes.
After taking off from Seattle he opened the aft door, deployed the airstair and parachuted.
In 1980 eight-year-old Brian Ingram, raking the riverbank at Tena Bar on the Columbia River to build a campfire, found $6,000 of the ransom.
The remaining money was never recovered.
His true identity and fate remain unknown.
